title: Core AI money circulation
scope: Public disclosures known by the snapshot; dates identify agreements or financial cutoffs, not proof of every later cash payment.
methodology: Arrows follow funding or buyer-to-supplier economics, not product delivery.
A matching triangle does not establish that identical dollars recycle, that demand is fake, or that revenue is artificial.
Do not sum investment amounts, contract ceilings, recognized revenue, receivables, facilities, guarantees and overlapping project totals.
Use actual external customer receipts, margins, cash collection, utilization, debt service and independent demand to assess sustainability.
OpenAI and Anthropic appear as private ecosystem nodes, not additions to the app's 100 public-stock universe.

edges.title: Strategic investment
edges.detail: Funding reported through June 30, 2026. Equity ownership is not cloud revenue.

edges.title: Azure services
edges.detail: October 2025 commitment, not cash paid. April 2026 terms permit all OpenAI products on other clouds; capped OpenAI-to-Microsoft revenue share continues through 2030.

edges.title: OpenAI preferred stock
edges.detail: $28.7B invested by June 30; remaining $21.3B funded after quarter-end, disclosed in Q2 filing.

edges.title: AWS capacity expansion
edges.detail: Incremental to prior $38B arrangement; includes roughly 2 GW Trainium. Contract value is not annual revenue or current payment.

edges.title: OpenAI financing round
edges.detail: Part of February round, later closed as committed capital. Individual funding timing not established here; do not add the earlier $100B letter-of-intent headline.

edges.title: Anthropic investment history
edges.detail: $8B historical convertible notes plus $10B preferred stock in Q2. Instrument conversions and valuation gains are not additional cash.

edges.title: Compute-linked financing
edges.detail: Original $20B capacity reduced by $5B Series H purchase. Further availability depends on compute-delivery milestones; draws may be convertible notes or stock.

edges.title: AWS compute agreement
edges.detail: Expanded Trainium and Graviton capacity agreement. Delivery and chip-performance obligations matter; not recognized AWS revenue.

edges.title: Anthropic equity commitment
edges.detail: Announced commitment. Anthropic's February Series G includes a portion of the previously announced Microsoft/NVIDIA investments; do not add both headlines.

edges.title: Anthropic equity commitment
edges.detail: Announced commitment; paid amount not established here. The Series G partly overlaps this commitment.

edges.title: Claude on Azure
edges.detail: Azure service purchase commitment, with additional capacity up to 1 GW. NVIDIA systems support this deployment; purchase dollars for hardware are undisclosed.

edges.title: Google TPU capacity
edges.amountLabel: Tens of billions; exact value undisclosed
edges.detail: October expansion targets up to one million TPUs. April 2026 Google/Broadcom agreement adds multiple GW starting 2027; no comparable incremental dollar amount given.

edges.title: CoreWeave stock purchase
edges.detail: Completed January 23: 22,935,780 Class A shares at $87.20. Equity issuance cash, not revenue.

edges.title: Residual cloud capacity
edges.detail: NVIDIA must buy qualifying unsold capacity through April 13, 2032, subject to delivery, availability and termination terms. Not an unconditional $6.3B cash transfer.

edges.title: GPU infrastructure purchases
edges.detail: CoreWeave filing identifies NVIDIA as GPU supplier and shareholder. Direct versus OEM-mediated purchase mix and transaction dollars are not quantified here.

edges.title: Model training and inference
edges.detail: Total includes March $11.9B, May $4B and September $6.5B agreements; do not sum the total with its components. Not current-year revenue.

edges.title: Dedicated GPU capacity
edges.detail: September 2025 contract through 2031, conditional on deployment and availability. Original disclosed values shown; later option exercise not verified here.

edges.title: Pre-funded share warrant
edges.detail: Nebius reports sale of a pre-funded Class A share warrant to NVIDIA; distinct from payment for GPU hardware.

edges.title: Stargate capacity partnership
edges.detail: Issuer describes up to 4.5 GW additional capacity under its July agreement. Overlapping Stargate investment totals are not additive.

edges.title: Credit support for OpenAI leases
edges.detail: August guarantee covers defined lease/power obligations for ~4.25 GW. Tenant defaults trigger payment; phases expected from FY2029. This is not cash spent, drawn debt or revenue.

supportingEdges.title: Actual related-party revenue
supportingEdges.detail: Includes commercial arrangements and revenue sharing; $6B receivable at June 30. Revenue is not proof of cash collection and is not incremental to all other contract figures.

supportingEdges.title: Blackwell infrastructure
supportingEdges.detail: NVIDIA reports thousands of Blackwell GPUs deployed on OCI. Monetary direction denotes buyer-to-supplier economics; reseller routing is not established.

supportingEdges.title: NVIDIA cloud platform
supportingEdges.detail: Nebius already deploys NVIDIA hardware; partnership targets more than 5 GW by end-2030. This target is not a purchase order or recognized revenue.

supportingEdges.title: GPU and contract-backed loan
supportingEdges.detail: DDTL 4.0 secured by infrastructure and customer contract; maturity March 2032. Drawn amount is not stated. MUFG/Morgan Stanley structure; Blackstone anchors.

supportingEdges.title: Monetizing installed GPU contracts
supportingEdges.detail: Secured by deployed GPUs and contracted customer cash flows; SOFR+2.5%, maturity October 2030. Source does not identify this facility's customer; do not assume Microsoft.

supportingEdges.title: PORTS campus leases
supportingEdges.detail: OpenAI affiliate is tenant. NVIDIA guarantee only covers defined portions; its $105B cap is not the total lease price.

cases.title: Investor, cloud vendor and revenue-share recipient
cases.summary: Microsoft finances OpenAI; OpenAI buys Azure services and generates reported Microsoft revenue.
cases.insight: Separate contracted demand, recognized revenue and receivables. Growth financed by new capital can be real, yet remains sensitive to the lab's eventual cash generation.
cases.limitation: No tracing of identical dollars. Microsoft's investment valuation is not investment cash, and recognized revenue is not profit.

cases.title: Funding customers of your own cloud
cases.summary: Amazon funds both OpenAI and Anthropic while both commit to long-term AWS capacity.
cases.insight: The commercial and financing exposures can weaken together if AI customers cannot cover compute costs from external demand.
cases.limitation: Different horizons and instruments; no valid single 'circulating dollars' total. Deliveries, conditions and funding milestones differ.

cases.title: Two investors, one NVIDIA-powered cloud route
cases.summary: Microsoft and NVIDIA back Anthropic, which contracts Azure capacity on NVIDIA systems.
cases.insight: One relationship supports model funding, cloud demand and accelerator demand. Hardware capacity alone does not reveal NVIDIA's transaction revenue.
cases.limitation: The supplier leg is documented technologically but not monetarily sized; Anthropic's other chip platforms diversify dependence.

cases.title: Supplier, shareholder and buyer of spare capacity
cases.summary: NVIDIA sells GPUs, invests in CoreWeave and backstops qualifying spare cloud capacity. Contract-backed loans finance deployment.
cases.insight: The key test is third-party utilization versus vendor support, alongside interest, GPU life, collateral and delivery obligations.
cases.limitation: Backstop value is conditional and cannot be added to equity, debt capacity or customer contract values as current sales.

cases.title: A hyperscaler contract becomes financing capacity
cases.summary: Microsoft contracts capacity; NVIDIA provides capital and hardware; lenders advance against deployed GPUs and customer cash flows.
cases.insight: Customer commitments can finance expansion into new enterprise workloads. Watch how much growth relies on deposits, refinancing and a few creditworthy buyers.
cases.limitation: The named Microsoft contract and July secured loan are not proven to be the same collateral pool. This is a financing chain, not a proven closed loop.

cases.title: Chip supplier underwrites the infrastructure tenant
cases.summary: NVIDIA's SB Energy guarantee supports OpenAI's future campus leases and an overwhelmingly NVIDIA-based site.
cases.insight: Credit support can unlock physical construction before tenant cash flows mature. The supplier gains deployment opportunities while accepting long-lived contingent risk.
cases.limitation: Ohio and Oracle projects are separate routes, not one contract. Guarantees are contingent exposure, not money already transferred.
